label: early original-phase input of w/n/q/k/g/s in sequences starting with h/1/m/0/f/z/j
explanation: Fires almost only during the original (input) phase: 99.5% of activation mass. Within that phase it fires at early positions t=2..5 (96% of active steps, peak at t=3), and never at t=0 or at t>=7. It is essentially silent in the delimiter and copy phases. Which steps fire depends jointly on the current input token and on the first token of the sequence. Strong input tokens are w (9.5x lift, 36% of mass), then n, q, k, g and s. Strong first tokens are h, 1, m, 0 and f, then z and j. It mostly fires on the first occurrence of the input token (93% of mass). The largest activations are w at t=3 in sequences that start with h or 1. Position alone gives recall 0.96 but precision 0.03. Adding the token sets raises dev F1 to about 0.52 (mass recall 0.65). The remaining activations are spread thinly over other token/prefix combinations (e.g. l, u, t, 2 inputs), so this is a graded, distributed code over position x input x first token rather than a clean monosemantic unit.

scorecard.summary: Graded preference over the current input token, by step (t=2: w, n, q, k; t=1: w; t=3: w, n, q, k) and the first original token (most: h, 1, m, 0, f, z; least: 2, k, t, w); timing cues that raise it most: L=3 & t=5, t=3, t=4.
